Capitalise on the GTF (ΔPV ≥ 0) is met today at +0.00. It stays met in S1 and S7 (0.00) and in S2, S4 and S5 (+6.36, +10.29, +14.85). It fails in S3 and S6 (-16.25, -16.29), where NGSA flies without us; no order on this board prevents that.

Ground 2, carrying an unselected engine: pass. launch_if_selected spends only if a live airframe puts P&W (code 2, 6 or 7) on the record this round and GTF2 is ready by that airframe's EIS: 2036 against 2037 or 2040. Ground 3, aggressive terms: pass. The GTF2 offer is on standard terms with no launch discount, concession or free upgrade. The durability kit is sold through MRO at value. The statement says 'on standard terms, with no launch discounts'.

Ground 4, booking upside before it is proven: pass.
- The statement books no selection, Rolls-Royce commitment, partner money or durability gain. Ready 2036 is launch + 6, a rule. 'Will not enter service until its durability is proven' is a condition, not a claim. The share figures (26.7% in 2026, 24.4% in 2029) are on the public bulletin.

recommendations.text: Public statement (Disclosure; recommendation only). The statement stays inside the limits: ready 2036 is launch + 6, durability is stated as a condition of entry into service, and no airframer date is given. However, the Board faces derivative claims over GTF oversight. Replace 'we have learned our lesson from the prior iterations of the GTF' with Eddy's wording on the industrial gaps on the GTF, keep the time-on-wing admission factual, and have counsel review the paragraph before release.

Write the 2035 cancel test for a triggered GTF2 to the Board's Premature exit rule. If launch_if_selected fires, a 2030 GTF2 can be cancelled only in 2035, with a write-off of 2 x 5/6 = $1.67B; from 2036 it is ready and can no longer be cancelled. While a live airframe's code still includes P&W and GTF2 can be ready by its EIS, the cancel row must beat the hold row in every plausible column, not only at Mitchill's weights. The test is judged on the remaining $0.33B, not the sunk $1.67B. P&W stands by a selecting customer.

Durability before entry into service. The margin is one year on a 2037 EIS (NGSA, 7-year fps) against past slips of one to two years on the Advantage, and four years on a 2040 EIS. If GTF2 is triggered, Eddy should bring the severe-environment test data and the full-life plan for life-limited parts to the Governance and Public Policy Committee before the 2035 round. If the data are late, the EIS moves and the testing does not. Advantage-level testing (3x the base programme) must fit inside the $2B bill; any overrun returns to Finance as a capital item.
If GTF2 is triggered, bring its whole-programme NPV to the Finance Committee every year, as UTC's board did with the GTF. Show the return against Do Nothing and against a buyback each time.

The standing promise to launch 'in any round an airframer selects it' is acceptable, but each round's order must still clear the return gate. A 2035 launch_if_selected is ready only in 2041. It can therefore serve 2035 airframes (EIS 2042 or 2045) but never a 2030 airframe (EIS 2037 or 2040). Say so in the 2035 case.

The unconditional franchise-defence launch was rightly left off. Its edge over launch_if_selected is -0.73 at Mitchill's weights and -0.64 at Calio's, against the Board's +$0.5B bar. The S3 and S6 exposure of about -$16.3B is real, but only a selection repairs it. Re-test the launch only if a public airframer statement makes NGSA-without-P&W the likely column before the orders seal.

Keep the Joint Venture with Rolls-Royce at hold in 2035 unless Rolls-Royce commits on the record or a live airframe names code 1, 4, 5 or 7. A Joint Venture formed in 2035 is ready in 2041, or in 2036 if a live 2030 GTF2 folds in. In any Joint Venture, share risk and investment, and keep the gear and core as P&W's own modules.
The dividend stays first and debt stays on its path back to pre-ASR levels. The one-time envelope stretch is unused; keep it in reserve.

board_review.note: The Board approves gtf2_solo: launch_if_selected, the order it recommended. Against hold it is 0 / +22.61 / 0 / +10.67 / +31.14 / 0 / 0, worth +$6.44B at Mitchill's weights and +$9.13B at Calio's, and never below hold. It commits the $2B only if an airframer selects P&W, the form the Board's doctrine prefers. GTF2 would be ready in 2036, ahead of an EIS of 2037 or 2040. If triggered, it costs $0.33B a year, 5.6% of the envelope, and the dividend and the debt path are untouched. No veto is unresolved, overrides is empty and premium_b is 0. The unconditional launch (edge -0.64 to -0.73) and the Joint Venture commit (-2.00 in S7) were correctly struck. Recommendations cover four points: the statement's GTF wording, given the derivative claims; the 2035 cancel test, written to the Premature exit rule; durability data before a 2037 EIS; and an annual NPV review if GTF2 is triggered.

rolls_royce.public_statement: So, plainly. Rolls-Royce will launch UltraFan for a new single-aisle in the round an airframer selects it. Not before. UltraFan is more efficient than any other engine available, and we have done the work without waiting. Entry into service no earlier than seven years from launch, with support and MRO in place, through partner shops, before entry into service. Our preference is partnership. The Joint Venture is open to Pratt & Whitney, and we commit when our partner does. No widebody UltraFan until a Re-engine is on the table. We won't do anything not profitable. rolls_royce.rationale:
DECISION. The orders are `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected`, `jv_with_pw: hold`, `ultrafan_wb: hold` and `t1000_upgrade: hold`. This is my framing proposal unchanged. McCabe, Watson and the Board's would-approve list all recommended the same orders.

1. GRID ROWS, SUBMITTED AGAINST HOLD (S1-S9, $B ΔPV)
- Submitted row, 'UltraFan NB if selected': 0.00 / +10.66 / 0.00 / +12.46 / +26.17 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00.
- Same row with the item at hold ('UltraFan NB: hold'): 0.00 in every column.
- Item value: 0 / +10.66 / 0 / +12.46 / +26.17 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.
- No other Board item is submitted.

2. WEIGHTS AND EXPECTED GAIN
- Weights A, confirmed by McCabe: S1 0.35, S2 0.05, S3 0.15, S4 0.03, S5 0.02, S6 0.10, S7 0.10, S8 0.12, S9 0.08.
- Selection totals 0.10 because nothing is on the public record (ExCo rule; the weights are inference, not my record).
- Expected gain: +1.43 on weights A, +5.48 uniform, +2.86 at a 0.20 signal.
- Worst column: 0.00 against an $8B bill. The unselected loss is 0.00. The option is never below hold under any weights.

3. ROWS TESTED AND REJECTED (expected on A / worst column)
- Unconditional Solo: -4.44 / -8.00.
- Trent 1000 upgrade alone: -0.84 / -0.98.
- `launch_if_selected` + upgrade: +0.09 / -0.98. The upgrade's own item value is -5.98 in S2, S4 and S5, beyond its bill.
- Joint Venture commit: -0.40 / -4.00 in S7.
- `launch_if_selected` + commit: +1.03 against +1.43.
- UltraFan WB: -3.38 / -4.00.
- The best expected plan inside the red lines is `launch_if_selected` alone, so the premium is $0.

4. TESTS
- Airframers first [RX-0058]: passes by construction. The option fires only if a live airframe selects a code that includes RR (1, 5 or 7) this round and UltraFan is ready by its entry into service.
- Four-part gate [RX-0030]: passes. The engine is differentiated, the market is large if an airframer selects us, the business is viable at +10.66 to +26.17, and the technology carries over to the widebody.
- Profitable or not at all: the triggered columns clear the +$2B bar 5 to 13 times. The unconditional launch fails it: it needs a selection probability of 0.49-0.54 and the record gives 0.10.
- Sure to deliver [RX-0124]: Watson confirms ready in 2037, the full seven years. That is zero margin against NGSA and fps 7-year (2037) and three years against fps 10-year or via Embraer (2040). Zero margin is a note, not compression.
- No options management [RX-0051]: nothing stands that no airframe can use. If untriggered, nothing is spent and nothing is left open. There is nothing to cancel.
- Widebody franchise: 58% in 2040, 2045 and 2050 in every column, 8 pp above the line.

5. CASH AS AN INPUT [RX-0042]
- Triggered, the Solo costs $8B over 7 years: about $1.14B, or GBP 0.84-0.85bn, a year.
- That is 22-23% of FY2026 free cash flow guidance (GBP 3.6-3.8bn) and 16-17% of the FY2028 target.
- It is funded from cash and redeployed inside a flat R&D envelope: no equity, no borrowing, leverage unchanged.

6. VETO CHECKS
- CFO: McCabe co-signs `launch_if_selected`. She withholds her signature (binding) on the unconditional Solo, a Joint Venture commit, UltraFan WB, and the upgrade beside the option. None of these is submitted. Her balance-sheet vetoes are not triggered.
- Civil: Watson invokes no veto. His conditions for the final statement are met. It names no entry into service before launch + 7 (it says 'no earlier than seven years from launch'). It says nothing on any airframer's dates. It keeps support and MRO before entry into service and adds 'through partner shops'. The support plan is a public other move.
- `overrides` is empty.

7. RED-LINE FLAGS
- McCabe and Watson both flagged the upgrade beside an ordered UltraFan as a company red-line breach. It is struck: the upgrade is held.
- No unconditional launch goes into an empty record.
- No Joint Venture commit goes in before P&W's.
- No UltraFan WB goes in without a Re-engine.
- No item can lose more than its own bill.
- No early date is disclosed anywhere.

8. WHERE I DEPART FROM MY PROFILE
- My profile's default was to fund the Trent 1000 upgrade in round 1. I hold it, and I say so plainly.
- On this board it earns nothing before a Re-engine or 2042: -0.98 in seven of nine columns.
- On the record it would put $5B of strain exactly where we are selected.
- Widebody already clears the line at 58%.
- Watson notes that a 2035 launch reaches 2042 just as well, so waiting costs no share year.
- The +$2B bar, the column weights and the partner-first ordering are company and team doctrine (inference), not my own record.

9. OBJECTIVE LINE, PLAINLY
- If the option triggers, 'enter the narrowbody market' is met (27.6% S2, 30.2% S4, 51.2% S5 of narrowbody engines in 2050) and widebody stays at 58%.
- But a triggered Solo commits $8B against the $4B bounded-narrowbody-risk line. I take that trade only on an airframer's selection.
- Holding the line strictly would mean holding, which costs the whole option ($1.43B on A, $5.48B uniform). I do not declare that as a premium: I choose the option.
- No upgrade is on the record, so no $5B strain is charged to this or any later narrowbody programme.
- If the option does not trigger, the narrowbody entry passes to 2035, the last round that can deliver by 2045. There the Joint Venture (formed in 2035, ready in 2041 against a 2042 entry into service) is the route that keeps within the $4B line.

Her four binding withholdings (unconditional Solo, Joint Venture commit before P&W's, UltraFan WB, upgrade beside the option) match items I had already rejected, so I revised nothing. I adopted her failure case, a code change before EIS that writes off $5.71B in a 2035 cancel, as an internal watch. I also adopted her plain statement that a triggered Solo breaches the $4B bounded-risk line. I take her pricing of strict compliance ($1.43B) as the CEO's call: I keep the option and declare no premium. I took her advice to hold the upgrade alone (-0.84, nothing before 2042) as well.

His widebody reading (58% to 2050; a 2035 upgrade reaches 2042 just as well) supports holding the upgrade. I keep his Joint Venture view on the table for 2035: formed then, ready in 2041 against a 2042 entry into service.

recommendations.text: Take the narrowbody option in its conditional form and on its own: `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected`. It costs nothing unless an airframer selects RR in 2030. If one does, it is worth +10.66 (NGSA, code 7), +12.46 (fps 10-yr, code 5) or +26.17 (both). This is likely the only round in which UltraFan Solo can meet a 2030 airframe: a 2035 launch is ready only in 2042, after a 2037 or 2040 EIS. An airframe first, but do not miss the airframe.

Hold the Trent 1000 upgrade this round. It counts only from the first Re-engine's EIS, or from 2042 if none comes, so a 2030 launch earns nothing earlier unless a Re-engine follows. The grid charges -0.98 in seven of nine columns. Once on the record it would put $5B of strain on any later UltraFan NB or Joint Venture, and breach the 'widebody never starved' line. Revisit it when a Re-engine, above all a rival-engined one, is on the record or when the narrowbody question is settled. If the ExCo still submits it, submit it alone, with about $0.84-0.98B in `premium_b` and the durability reason.

Partner first, in the right order. Do not commit to the Joint Venture into an empty record: in S7 it forms with no airframe and loses its full $4B. Say publicly that the Joint Venture is open to Pratt & Whitney, and commit once P&W's commitment is on the record or an airframer names a P&W code. Note too that a triggered Solo commits $8B against the $4B bounded-risk line. The ExCo should state that plainly in `rationale`, and the Joint Venture is the route that keeps within it later.

The public statement should be few, conditional and binding words. UltraFan is ready seven years after launch, so no entry into service before 2037 for a 2030 launch. Say nothing on any airframer's dates, name support and MRO in place before EIS, and say the Joint Venture is open to P&W. Make no promise of a widebody UltraFan until a Re-engine is on the record.

Show us the reasonable worst case for every item, not the base case. That means each item's worst plausible column against its own bill, McCabe's column weights and the selection probability used (we read 0.1 with nothing on the record), her co-signature, and Watson's ready year against each airframe's EIS.

UltraFan WB waits for a Re-engine on the record. Widebody share holds at 58% to 2050 on every hold row and no rival-engined Re-engine exists, so the widebody franchise test is not triggered this round. If a 787 or A350 Re-engine appears in the bulletin, bring UltraFan WB or the upgrade back to us, one programme at a time.

frame.question: So, the 2030 question, in cash and quality of earnings. The public record is empty: no fps, no NGSA, no engine selection, no Pratt & Whitney commitment, no Re-engine. What do we put on the table that pays if an airframer picks Rolls-Royce this round and costs nothing if it does not? Concretely: do we take UltraFan NB as `launch_if_selected` (worst column 0.00; +10.66, +12.46 or +26.17 if selected)? And do we spend anything this round on the widebody (Trent 1000 upgrade, UltraFan WB) or on the Joint Venture? Each of those loses money in most of the grid's columns. Frankly, the trap this round is buying activity. "We won't do anything not profitable. I will say that categorically." [RX-0058] Choices, not options management [RX-0051].
frame.situation:

- No fps and no NGSA, so there are no engine codes. No 787 Re-engine and no A350 Re-engine. No Joint Venture commitment by P&W or by us. No CFM/GE or P&W engine launch.

TIMING THAT MATTERS (rules):
- Entry into service from a 2030 launch: NGSA 2037; fps 7-year 2037; fps 10-year or via Embraer 2040.

- A Joint Venture formed in 2030 is ready in 2036. P&W is not committed, so it cannot form.
- An UltraFan launched in 2035 is ready only in 2042, so it misses any airframe launched in 2030.

- Enter the narrowbody market: NOT MET (0.0% in 2045 and 2050).
- Keep widebody dominance: MET (58.0% at worst).
- Bounded narrowbody risk (own narrowbody money of $4B or less): MET ($0.0B).
- Widebody never starved: MET ($0 strain).

GRID COLUMNS:
- S1: rivals hold.
- S2: NGSA selects us (code 7).

- S5: both launch, and we are on both.

tests.threshold: Expected gain over hold of at least +$2B. That is the team bar for rounds before the 2035 round, the last slot that still delivers by 2045.
tests.numbers: Row 'UltraFan NB Solo' minus hold: -8.00 / +10.66 / -3.69 / +12.46 / +26.17 / -1.15 / -8.00 / -8.00 / -8.00. tests.threshold: P&W's commitment must be on the public record, and the expected gain must be above 0.

In S7 it forms with no airframe to fly it. Expected gain: -0.40 (A), -0.44 (uniform), -1.00 (P&W-heavy). It is never above 0 on any weight set. Beside launch_if_selected it is the same: row 'if selected + commit to JV' minus 'if selected' is -4.00 in S7, so +1.03 against +1.43 (A).

tests.name: Hurdle (co-signature): ultrafan_wb launch
tests.threshold: The row must beat hold, or the gap must be declared as a premium within $3B. The Board caps an UltraFan WB premium at $1B. A Re-engine must be on the public record.

The shortfall is above the $1B sub-cap, and no 787 or A350 Re-engine is on the record. Beside launch_if_selected the item is -4.00 / -9.00 / -4.00 / -9.00 / -9.00 / -4.00 / -4.00 / -0.90 / -0.90, which is -3.88 (A). The extra loss is the $5B strain in S2, S4 and S5.

tests.numbers: Alone, row 'UltraFan NB: hold + T1000 upgrade' minus hold: -0.98 in S1-S7 and -0.29 in S8-S9. Expected gain: -0.84 (A), -0.83 (uniform). It does not beat hold. Beside launch_if_selected, row 'if selected + T1000' minus 'if selected': -0.98 / -5.98 / -0.98 / -5.98 / -5.98 / -0.98 / -0.98 / -0.29 / -0.29, which is -1.34 (A). The plan's row is +0.09 (A) against +1.43 without the upgrade.

tests.name: Unselected downside: recommended orders (launch_if_selected alone, all else hold)
tests.threshold: State the worst column of every row. Nothing is spent unless the order triggers. No item may lose more than its own bill in any plausible column.
tests.numbers: launch_if_selected: worst 0.00 in S1, S3, S6, S7, S8 and S9, against an $8B bill. Unselected loss 0.00, confirmed. The CFO-side failure case outside the grid: the grid assumes nobody moves after 2030, but an airframer may change its code before the 2037 EIS. A triggered 2030 Solo cancelled in 2035 writes off $8B x 5/7 = $5.71B. Kept as an orphan, it loses up to its $8B bill. Both outcomes stay within its own bill. Worst columns of the other rows, for the record: unconditional Solo -8.00, its full bill (S1, S7, S8, S9); Joint Venture commit -4.00 (S7); UltraFan WB -4.00 alone and -9.00 beside the option; upgrade -0.98 alone.

A 2030 upgrade is ready by 2033, so it can no longer be cancelled in the 2035 round. Its $5B strain would then be locked in against any later Solo or Joint Venture (inference from the rules).

tests.name: Capex a year in GBP
tests.threshold: For information only; my evidence sets no threshold.
tests.numbers: UltraFan NB Solo (only if triggered): $8B over 7 years is $1.14B a year. That is about £0.84bn at 1.36 $/£ (2026) or £0.85bn at 1.34 (2028 on). It is 22-23% of FY2026 FCF guidance of £3.6-3.8bn and 16-17% of the FY2028 target of £5.0-5.3bn. It is roughly double my 'more than £400 million' half-year investment run rate. Joint Venture share: $4B over 6 years, about £0.49bn a year (13-14% of FY2026 FCF). UltraFan WB: $4B over 6 years, about £0.49bn a year. Trent 1000 upgrade: $2B over 3 years, about £0.49bn a year. Nothing is spent this round unless an airframer selects us.

tests.name: Flat R&D envelope (advice)
tests.threshold: Report any overlap and the $5B strain, which the grid already includes. Red lines: no UltraFan NB Solo beside UltraFan WB unless both are selected, and no upgrade while an UltraFan is ordered or in development. New money is redeployed, not added (inference).
tests.numbers: launch_if_selected alone: no overlap and $0 strain in every column (objective table: $0B strain on row 'UltraFan NB if selected'). With the upgrade or UltraFan WB beside it, the $5B strain hits S2, S4 and S5, and the red line is breached. If triggered, about £0.84bn a year has to be found inside a broadly flat gross R&D envelope by redeploying, not by adding.

tests.name: Balance sheet

tests.numbers: A triggered Solo costs about £0.84bn a year against FCF of £3.6-3.8bn (2026) rising to £5.0-5.3bn (2028). It is funded from cash. No equity, no borrowing, and leverage is unchanged (board debt $40B on EV $110B). No balance-sheet veto applies this round.

tests.name: Joint Venture cost against Solo
tests.threshold: Read the Joint Venture row against hold column by column. The fold write-off and share equalisation are already in the grid and are not deducted again (inference).
tests.numbers: The Joint Venture cannot form in 2030 because P&W has not committed, and no Solo is live. For reference, a Joint Venture costs $4B against the Solo's $8B, half the bill, and keeps us inside the $4B bounded-risk line. If a triggered 2030 Solo were folded into a Joint Venture formed in 2035, spend to date would be $8B x 5/7 = $5.71B. That counts against the $4B line, and the $1.71B beyond our $4B share is written off. Our narrowbody share would also be equalised with P&W's. Keep the Joint Venture open, publicly, as the 2035 route: formed then, it is ready in 2041.

tests.name: Short payback first
tests.threshold: State when each order starts to earn. The brief gives no payback years (inference).
tests.numbers: A 2030 UltraFan NB, if triggered, is ready in 2037 and earns from the airframe's EIS: 2037 for NGSA or fps 7-yr, 2040 for fps 10-yr or via Embraer. That is 7-10 years after launch. A 2030 upgrade earns 3 years after launch but not before the first Re-engine's EIS: no earlier than 2035, and 2042 if no Re-engine comes, which is 12 years. A Joint Venture earns 6 years after formation and cannot form this round. UltraFan WB earns only once a re-engined 787 or A350 is in service.

tests.name: Premium
tests.threshold: Price every doctrine or objective premium in $B. Above $3B a round, the PV-best order applies. UltraFan WB is capped at $1B.

Objective note: a triggered Solo commits $8B against the $4B bounded-risk line in S2, S4 and S5. Keeping that line strictly this round means holding, which costs the whole option: $1.43B (A), $5.48B (uniform). Whether to declare that is the CEO's call; I price it. If the upgrade were funded alone instead, the premium would be $0.84-0.98B against hold, but $2.27B (A) to $6.30B (uniform) against the PV-best plan.

vetoes.plan: ultrafan_nb_solo: launch (unconditional)

vetoes.plan: ultrafan_wb: launch

vetoes.plan: t1000_upgrade: launch alone (all else hold)

vetoes.plan: Balance-sheet vetoes (equity raise, leverage above about 1.5x, levering up for buybacks)
vetoes.ground: Not triggered. A triggered Solo costs about £0.84bn a year, funded from FCF of £3.6-3.8bn (2026) rising to £5.0-5.3bn (2028). It needs no equity, no borrowing and no change in leverage.

cfo.would_change_mind_if:
Delivered numbers and an announced customer would change my view.
- **Airframer names UltraFan:** if NGSA or fps names a code with RR on the public record, the selection probability goes to about 0.6. On this grid an unconditional Solo would then be about +3.2 (NGSA) to +4.3 (fps) expected, clearing the +$2B bar. I would co-sign a launch against that record.
- **P&W commits:** if P&W's Joint Venture commitment is on the record and the commit row is above 0 against hold, I co-sign a jv_with_pw commit. This is the route that keeps us inside the $4B line.
- **Re-engine announced:** if a 787 or A350 Re-engine is on the record, I would re-test UltraFan WB or the upgrade, one programme at a time and only with no narrowbody programme ordered or live. A350 first: it protects the widebody base I manage to.
- **Upgrade row:** if a later grid shows the upgrade beating hold, I fund it.
- **Triggered option, then a code change:** if launch_if_selected triggers and the airframer later drops RR before EIS, I would book the cancel arithmetic ($5.71B in 2035), not the sunk cost.
- **Selected columns weaken:** if a later grid shows the selected columns falling below +$2B, I would withhold even on the conditional form.

tests.name: Ready by EIS
tests.threshold: UltraFan NB ready (launch + 7) no later than the EIS of the airframe that selects it. Zero margin passes, with a note. Joint Venture engine ready at formation + 6, or earlier only with a folded Solo that is further along. A fail is advice, not a veto.
tests.numbers: UltraFan NB launch_if_selected in 2030 is ready in 2037. NGSA 2030 EIS 2037: margin 0 (pass, note). fps 7-yr 2037: margin 0 (pass, note). fps 10-yr or via Embraer 2040: margin +3. The trigger fires only if UltraFan is ready by the EIS, so it passes by construction. Seven full development years, not compressed. Joint Venture: it cannot form in 2030 because P&W has not committed. If formed in 2030 it would be ready in 2036. Formed in 2035 it is ready in 2041, which misses a 2037 or 2040 EIS unless it folds in a 2030 Solo (ready 2037). An UltraFan launched in 2035 is ready in 2042 and misses every 2030 airframe. For a 2035 airframe (EIS 2042, or 2045 for fps 10-yr): a 2035 UltraFan has margin 0 or +3; a 2035 Joint Venture has margin +1 or +4.

tests.name: No early date
tests.threshold: No disclosed EIS or ready date earlier than launch + 7 (UltraFan NB), launch + 6 (UltraFan WB) or formation + 6 (Joint Venture). Applies to the statement and to public other moves.
tests.numbers: Draft line: 'Entry into service no earlier than seven years from launch', which is 2037 for a 2030 trigger (launch + 7). Nothing on any airframer's dates. No Joint Venture date and no UltraFan WB date. I re-check at step 4 against the final statement and the public other moves.

tests.name: Support before EIS
tests.threshold: RR has no narrowbody MRO scale, so a support plan through partner shops must exist before any narrowbody EIS (inference)
tests.numbers: The draft statement says 'Support and MRO in place before entry into service'. The plan: a partner-shop network on the Singapore Joint Venture model, repair technology qualified in those shops, a spare-engine pool, and an early-years intervention team. Internal gates, not public (inference): partner agreements set when the trigger fires (2030), capacity qualified by 2036, live by the first EIS in 2037. Pass on condition that the final statement keeps the support line, adds 'through partner shops', and a public other move names the plan. If the final orders drop it, that is veto ground (c).

tests.name: Engineering load
tests.threshold: A narrowbody project and a widebody project on the record together cost $5B of strain. Red lines: no UltraFan WB beside an NB Solo unless both are selected; no Trent 1000 upgrade while an UltraFan is ordered or in development (seat and company rule, inference).
tests.numbers: launch_if_selected alone carries $0 strain in all nine columns. Beside the upgrade there is $5B of strain in S2, S4 and S5; the upgrade's item value is -0.98/-5.98/-0.98/-5.98/-5.98/-0.98/-0.98/-0.29/-0.29. Beside UltraFan WB there is $5B in S2, S4 and S5; that item is -4.00/-9.00/-4.00/-9.00/-9.00/-4.00/-4.00/-0.90/-0.90. Overlap if the trigger fires: UltraFan NB in development 2030-2037, against the upgrade 2030-2033 or UltraFan WB 2030-2036. The recommended orders hold no overlap. History: RR had the resources for only 3 of 4 engines in 2014, and running 3 programmes at once in 2016 was 'unprecedented'.

tests.name: Capacity and suppliers
tests.threshold: State RR engines a year from the brief. The board has no capacity limit, so this is not applicable unless the brief reports a constraint. A narrowbody ramp needs partner MRO and high-performing supplier capacity (advice).
tests.numbers: Hold row: 0 NB and 197 WB engines a year, 2026-2060 (brief §1). If triggered, RR's NB share in 2050 is 27.6% (S2), 30.2% (S4) or 51.2% (S5). At the board's 4,000 NB engines a year that is an indicative ceiling of about 1,100-2,050 a year; supply limits keep it lower while NGSA or fps ramps up. Compare 197 WB today and my midterm OE ramp of 300-350 a year. For MRO load I use my figure of 1,100-1,200 shop visits, not the 1,400-1,500 definition. Advice: place gearbox sizing, castings and forgings with high-performing suppliers (GBP 685M of GBP 2.5B in 2023 went to that group), and build MRO through partner shops.

tests.name: Widebody dominance
tests.threshold: RR widebody engine share of at least 50% in 2040, 2045 and 2050 on the brief's projection
tests.numbers: launch_if_selected row: 58.0% in 2040, 2045 and 2050 in every column, 8 pp above the line. Hold: 58% every year. Upgrade row: 58/63/63, because with no Re-engine it counts only from 2042. UltraFan WB reaches 68% in 2050 only in S8 and S9. No widebody move is needed to hold the line this round.

tests.name: Technology pull-through
tests.threshold: An idle or untriggered UltraFan still feeds the Trent fleet. Noted qualitatively; grid values never adjusted.
tests.numbers: Untriggered, the self-funded narrowbody demonstrator and UltraFan technology keep feeding Trent time on wing. Not priced; no grid adjustment.

vetoes.plan: ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected, with the CEO's draft statement
vetoes.ground: Not invoked. Zero margin (ready 2037 against an NGSA or fps 7-yr EIS of 2037) uses the full launch + 7 development time. It is a note, not compressed maturity. I would invoke the binding Civil veto at the step-4 check only if the final statement or a public other move (a) names an EIS or ready date before 2037, (b) counts on UltraFan entering service before its ready year, or (c) drops support before EIS and has no partner-shop plan. The ground rests on attributed transcript turns.

vetoes.plan: t1000_upgrade: launch beside ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected
vetoes.ground: Not a Civil veto ground. It breaks the company red line (no upgrade while an UltraFan is ordered or in development) and adds $5B of strain: the item is -5.98 in S2, S4 and S5, beyond its own $2B bill. If submitted I flag it at the veto check as a red-line breach; the CEO strikes it.

vetoes.plan: ultrafan_wb: launch
vetoes.ground: Advice only. No Re-engine is on the record. The item is -4.00 in S1-S7 and -0.90 in S8-S9; beside launch_if_selected it is -9.00 in S2, S4 and S5. Beside a triggered NB Solo it is a red-line breach. A 2030 launch is ready in 2036, a year after a 2030 Re-engine's 2035 EIS.

vetoes.plan: jv_with_pw: commit
vetoes.ground: Advice only. No maturity ground. It cannot form without P&W, and it costs -4.00 in S7, where it forms with no airframe. If formed, the engine is ready at formation + 6 and no earlier date may be stated. Solo against the Joint Venture is the CEO's call.

vetoes.plan: ultrafan_nb_solo: launch (unconditional)
vetoes.ground: Not a Civil veto ground on maturity, since it would be ready in 2037. But with no airframe it would need a support plan before EIS with nothing yet to support. Its -8.00 in S1, S7, S8 and S9 is McCabe's and the Board's ground, not mine.

ops.would_change_mind_if:
Any of these would change my view:
(1) Test or demonstrator evidence that UltraFan NB maturity would slip past launch + 7. Then a zero-margin trigger against an NGSA or fps 7-yr EIS of 2037 needs a fresh look, and we tell the airframer early rather than squeeze testing.
(2) A 787 or A350 Re-engine on the public record. That brings the Trent 1000 upgrade or UltraFan WB back to the table, one programme at a time and only once the narrowbody question is settled. With no Re-engine, a 2035 upgrade still counts from 2042.
(3) P&W's Joint Venture commitment on the record, or a code 4 or P&W selection. That makes the Joint Venture the better-margin route: formed in 2035 it is ready in 2041, against a 2042 EIS.
(4) A final statement or public other move with an EIS earlier than launch + 7, or without support before EIS through partner shops. I would invoke the binding Civil veto.
(5) Named airline commitments for a Rolls-Royce narrowbody engine.
ops.memo:
Tufan, Helen: my Civil tests on the 2030 orders.

Readiness. UltraFan NB triggered this round is ready in 2037: zero margin against NGSA and a 7-year fps (2037), three years against a 10-year fps or Embraer (2040). That is the full seven years of development, not a compressed one, so it passes. Zero margin means the testing schedule never bends to an airframer's date; if testing slips, we tell the airframer early. We pace the programme properly.

Strain. `launch_if_selected` alone carries no strain in any column. The upgrade beside it is -5.98 in S2, S4 and S5, exactly where we win; UltraFan WB beside it is -9.00. Both break our red lines. Hold them.

Support. We have no narrowbody MRO scale. The trigger needs a partner-shop plan on the Singapore Joint Venture model, with repair capability, spares and an intervention team in place before the first entry into service. Please add "through partner shops" to the statement.

Widebody. 58% in 2040, 2045 and 2050 on this row, against a 50% line. With no Re-engine the upgrade counts only from 2042, and a 2035 launch reaches 2042 just as well. Waiting costs no share year.

Joint Venture. Formed in 2035, it is ready in 2041, a year ahead of a 2035 airframe's 2042 entry into service. That is the better-margin route if 2030 passes us by. Your call.

Statement: no early date, nothing on airframer dates. I concur; no veto. We're clearly aligned as one Rolls-Royce.

other_moves.move: Standard commercial terms only
other_moves.detail: No concessions to buy narrowbody or widebody share. Win-win terms, value remunerated, and every new contract goes through the Investment Committee [RX-0081, RX-0055, RX-0097].

other_moves.move: Narrowbody support plan through partner shops
other_moves.detail: If an airframer selects UltraFan, the support plan goes live: a partner-shop network on the Singapore Joint Venture model, repair technology qualified in those shops, a spare-engine pool and an early-years intervention team, all in place before entry into service [RX-0283, RX-0287]. No dates are disclosed.

other_moves.move: Joint Venture open to Pratt & Whitney
other_moves.detail: Rolls-Royce commits to the Joint Venture once Pratt & Whitney's commitment is on the public record, on terms that credit the technology Rolls-Royce brings [RX-0072, RX-0118]. No Joint Venture date is disclosed.

other_moves.move: UltraFan technology demonstration and Trent time-on-wing work continue
other_moves.detail: The self-funded UltraFan narrowbody technology work continues inside a flat R&D envelope [RX-0094, RX-0214]. The durability and time-on-wing programme on the installed Trent fleet continues [RX-0123]. No new programme is launched.

other_moves.move: Internal readiness gates (not public)
other_moves.detail: Watson's gates, which apply only if the option triggers: partner-shop agreements signed in the trigger year, capacity qualified by 2036, support live by the first entry into service. Gearbox, casting and forging capacity pre-qualified with high-performing suppliers. No spend before the trigger. Testing never bends to an airframer's date; if maturity slips, we tell the airframer early.

other_moves.move: Cancel-arithmetic watch (not public)
other_moves.detail: If the option triggers and the airframer later drops Rolls-Royce from its code before entry into service, McCabe books the cancel arithmetic ($8B x 5/7 = $5.71B for a 2035 cancel), not the sunk cost, and the orphan programme is cancelled ('that activity is gone') [R-1573].

decision.public_statement: So, plainly. Rolls-Royce will launch UltraFan for a new single-aisle in the round an airframer selects it. Not before. UltraFan is more efficient than any other engine available, and we have done the work without waiting. Entry into service no earlier than seven years from launch, with support and MRO in place, through partner shops, before entry into service. Our preference is partnership. The Joint Venture is open to Pratt & Whitney, and we commit when our partner does. No widebody UltraFan until a Re-engine is on the table. We won't do anything not profitable. I will say that categorically.
decision.rationale:
DECISION. The orders are `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected`, `jv_with_pw: hold`, `ultrafan_wb: hold` and `t1000_upgrade: hold`. This is my framing proposal unchanged. McCabe, Watson and the Board's would-approve list all recommended the same orders.

1. GRID ROWS, SUBMITTED AGAINST HOLD (S1-S9, $B ΔPV)
- Submitted row, 'UltraFan NB if selected': 0.00 / +10.66 / 0.00 / +12.46 / +26.17 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00.
- Same row with the item at hold ('UltraFan NB: hold'): 0.00 in every column.
- Item value: 0 / +10.66 / 0 / +12.46 / +26.17 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.
- No other Board item is submitted.

2. WEIGHTS AND EXPECTED GAIN
- Weights A, confirmed by McCabe: S1 0.35, S2 0.05, S3 0.15, S4 0.03, S5 0.02, S6 0.10, S7 0.10, S8 0.12, S9 0.08.
- Selection totals 0.10 because nothing is on the public record (ExCo rule; the weights are inference, not my record).
- Expected gain: +1.43 on weights A, +5.48 uniform, +2.86 at a 0.20 signal.
- Worst column: 0.00 against an $8B bill. The unselected loss is 0.00. The option is never below hold under any weights.

3. ROWS TESTED AND REJECTED (expected on A / worst column)
- Unconditional Solo: -4.44 / -8.00.
- Trent 1000 upgrade alone: -0.84 / -0.98.
- `launch_if_selected` + upgrade: +0.09 / -0.98. The upgrade's own item value is -5.98 in S2, S4 and S5, beyond its bill.
- Joint Venture commit: -0.40 / -4.00 in S7.
- `launch_if_selected` + commit: +1.03 against +1.43.
- UltraFan WB: -3.38 / -4.00.
- The best expected plan inside the red lines is `launch_if_selected` alone, so the premium is $0.

4. TESTS
- Airframers first [RX-0058]: passes by construction. The option fires only if a live airframe selects a code that includes RR (1, 5 or 7) this round and UltraFan is ready by its entry into service.
- Four-part gate [RX-0030]: passes. The engine is differentiated, the market is large if an airframer selects us, the business is viable at +10.66 to +26.17, and the technology carries over to the widebody.
- Profitable or not at all: the triggered columns clear the +$2B bar 5 to 13 times. The unconditional launch fails it: it needs a selection probability of 0.49-0.54 and the record gives 0.10.
- Sure to deliver [RX-0124]: Watson confirms ready in 2037, the full seven years. That is zero margin against NGSA and fps 7-year (2037) and three years against fps 10-year or via Embraer (2040). Zero margin is a note, not compression.
- No options management [RX-0051]: nothing stands that no airframe can use. If untriggered, nothing is spent and nothing is left open. There is nothing to cancel.
- Widebody franchise: 58% in 2040, 2045 and 2050 in every column, 8 pp above the line.

5. CASH AS AN INPUT [RX-0042]
- Triggered, the Solo costs $8B over 7 years: about $1.14B, or GBP 0.84-0.85bn, a year.
- That is 22-23% of FY2026 free cash flow guidance (GBP 3.6-3.8bn) and 16-17% of the FY2028 target.
- It is funded from cash and redeployed inside a flat R&D envelope: no equity, no borrowing, leverage unchanged.

6. VETO CHECKS
- CFO: McCabe co-signs `launch_if_selected`. She withholds her signature (binding) on the unconditional Solo, a Joint Venture commit, UltraFan WB, and the upgrade beside the option. None of these is submitted. Her balance-sheet vetoes are not triggered.
- Civil: Watson invokes no veto. His conditions for the final statement are met. It names no entry into service before launch + 7 (it says 'no earlier than seven years from launch'). It says nothing on any airframer's dates. It keeps support and MRO before entry into service and adds 'through partner shops'. The support plan is a public other move.
- `overrides` is empty.

7. RED-LINE FLAGS
- McCabe and Watson both flagged the upgrade beside an ordered UltraFan as a company red-line breach. It is struck: the upgrade is held.
- No unconditional launch goes into an empty record.
- No Joint Venture commit goes in before P&W's.
- No UltraFan WB goes in without a Re-engine.
- No item can lose more than its own bill.
- No early date is disclosed anywhere.

8. WHERE I DEPART FROM MY PROFILE
- My profile's default was to fund the Trent 1000 upgrade in round 1. I hold it, and I say so plainly.
- On this board it earns nothing before a Re-engine or 2042: -0.98 in seven of nine columns.
- On the record it would put $5B of strain exactly where we are selected.
- Widebody already clears the line at 58%.
- Watson notes that a 2035 launch reaches 2042 just as well, so waiting costs no share year.
- The +$2B bar, the column weights and the partner-first ordering are company and team doctrine (inference), not my own record.

9. OBJECTIVE LINE, PLAINLY
- If the option triggers, 'enter the narrowbody market' is met (27.6% S2, 30.2% S4, 51.2% S5 of narrowbody engines in 2050) and widebody stays at 58%.
- But a triggered Solo commits $8B against the $4B bounded-narrowbody-risk line. I take that trade only on an airframer's selection.
- Holding the line strictly would mean holding, which costs the whole option ($1.43B on A, $5.48B uniform). I do not declare that as a premium: I choose the option.
- No upgrade is on the record, so no $5B strain is charged to this or any later narrowbody programme.
- If the option does not trigger, the narrowbody entry passes to 2035, the last round that can deliver by 2045. There the Joint Venture (formed in 2035, ready in 2041 against a 2042 entry into service) is the route that keeps within the $4B line.

recommendations.text: If the option triggers, protect the programme. Pace testing to the full seven years. Zero margin against a 2037 NGSA or fps 7-year EIS means the schedule never bends to an airframer's date, and if maturity slips, tell the airframer early. Report Watson's ready year against the selecting airframe's EIS to the Safety, Energy Transition & Tech Committee every round. Have the partner-shop support agreements signed in the trigger year, as his internal gates require.

If the option triggers, nothing goes beside it on the widebody. With a live UltraFan NB, the Trent 1000 upgrade or UltraFan WB would bring the one-off $5B strain into the very columns where we were selected. It would also breach the company rule against an upgrade while an UltraFan is in development. One big programme at a time, inside a broadly flat R&D envelope. Find the GBP 0.84-0.85bn a year by redeploying spend, not adding to it.

If the option does not trigger, 2035 is the last round that can deliver narrowbody share by 2045. Bring us the Joint Venture route first. Formed in 2035, it is ready in 2041 against a 2042 EIS, and it stays inside the $4B bounded-risk line. Commit only once P&W's commitment is on the public record or a live airframe's code includes P&W, and with a weighted value at or above 0. Otherwise take `launch_if_selected` again into any 2035 airframe: ready in 2042, zero margin against a 2042 EIS.

Plan the orphan case now. If a triggered programme loses its airframe before EIS (the code drops RR), bring us the cancel promptly, and book the write-off arithmetic rather than the sunk cost: $8B x 5/7 = $5.71B for a 2035 cancel, within its bill. A programme a live airframe still flies is never cancelled.

Keep the widebody core under watch, not under spend. Trent holds 58% in 2040, 2045 and 2050 on every row, with no Re-engine on the record, so the widebody franchise test is not triggered. If a 787 or A350 Re-engine appears, above all a rival-engined one, bring the Trent 1000 upgrade or UltraFan WB back to us. Bring only one of them, and only if no narrowbody programme is live or could be triggered that round. Show any shortfall in `premium_b`, within $3B in all and $1B for UltraFan WB. Watson notes that a 2035 upgrade still counts from 2042, so waiting costs no share year today.

Keep the public statement this disciplined. Use no date earlier than launch plus development years, nothing on any airframer's dates, support before EIS, and 'we commit when our partner does'. Rest any efficiency claim on demonstrated results. Next round, update the column weights from the bulletin: 0.6 where an airframer names UltraFan, 0.35 with the engine open, 0.2 for a signal. Show each item's worst column against its bill, as this package did.

board_review.note: Product safety is and always must be our most important priority, and this package respects it. It allows seven full years of development, discloses no early date, and puts support through partner shops before entry into service. We approve the one Board item, `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected`. It spends nothing unless an airframer selects us this round. If one does, it is worth +10.66, +12.46 or +26.17: +1.43 weighted on McCabe's weights, with a worst column of 0.00 against an $8B bill. McCabe co-signs, Watson invokes no veto, and there is no premium, no overlap and no override. An airframe first, but we will not miss the airframe. We note plainly that a triggered Solo commits $8B against the $4B bounded-risk line, and we accept that only on a selection. We do not want to underestimate the risks: if it triggers, nothing goes beside it on the widebody, and testing never bends to an airframer's date.
